description: Sustained rain caused the landing strip to become saturated, raising serious questions about whether the Twin Otter could extract the crew.
response: The Commander monitored and photographed the strip from mid-mission; images were sent to the charter. The strip remained marginally usable and extraction was successful.
lesson: From mid-mission, assign someone to check and photograph the landing strip every 2 days. Send images proactively to the charter operator. Know the ground condition threshold below which they will refuse to land.
source_citation: SRC-hypatia-iii-brief, Part IV – Incident and emergency register, §4.2 Meteorological incidents, lines 605-610. Register Crew tag: 'Mars160'. Sol: qualitative cue only ('from mid-mission'); no sol structure given for Mars160 in this source — placeholder. Confidence (C) rationale: Commander-narrative account (monitoring/photography actions); risk was averted rather than materializing, classified Near-Miss on that basis.
